Comments: On 8/13/2026, the Department conducted follow-up inspection of Diversified's Holchin 2 plugged well site located in North Union Township, Fayette County. This inspection regards violations issued in IR 4181294 and IR 4240230. At the time of this inspection, the E and S/Restoration Plan was on-site. The former access road and well site has established additional vegetative growth coverage since the Department's previous surface inspection on 6/30/2026. However, the previously identified disturbance due to third-party livestock remains ongoing in the restored area. All temporary E and S BMPs have been removed. No equipment or waste are observed on-site. An erected monument with the API number is observed on-site.A Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) was submitted to the Department by the Operator on 7/24/2026. A signed and notarized Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration was submitted with the WSRR, where the landowner requested to waive well site restoration. Further review conducted by the Department found that an outdated Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration form was submitted with the WSRR. The current version has a revision date of 06/2026. The form submitted by the operator contains a revision date of 07/2025.Therefore, the WSRR was denied in IR 4257555, as the Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration is administratively deficient.Based on todays inspection, the violations issued in IR 4181294 and IR 4240230 will remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/11/2024 to CNX GAS CO LLC in Wayne Township, Greene county. CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CNX GAS CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/11/2024
Violation Code: CSL 301 - PROHIBITION AGAINST DISCHARGE OF INDUSTRIAL WASTES - Industrial waste discharged into Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8204433
Permit API: 059-22716
Unconventional: No
County: Greene
Municipality: Wayne Township
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 10/11/2024
Comments: On 10/11/2024, I conducted an inspection at the Blacksville I BIP32 Well in Wayne Township, Greene County in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug a well The NOI was received by The Department on 9/9/2024 and 10/1/2024 due to plugging schedule changes.On site at the time of inspection were contractors associated with well plugging. The contractors indicated that the plugging rig was set up on 10/8/2024, and they expected the plugging operation to take 3 days to complete.While on site I observed the following:-The access road appeared to be in generally good condition. I recommend that the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) installed along the access road receive additional aggregate if contractors expect to be on site for additional time (Photos 1-6).-I observed a silt fence filled with sediment at STA 14+00. I observed sediment that bypassed the silt fence at STA 14+00 and entered a stream identified by E and S plans as UNT to Dunkard Creek. Scouring left of the culvert outlet was evident where sediment bypassed the silt fence. Sediment accumulation was evident throughout the streambed and significant sediment buildup was present within the culvert outlet. I followed sediment within the streambed for approximately 50 feet below the culvert outlet (Photos 7-15).-I observed no sediment accumulation above the timber matting crossing at the culvert inlet, indicating that sediment entered the stream where it bypassed the perimeter silt fence (Photo 16).-A material stockpile staged along the access road at STA 15+00 was bordered by reinforced silt fence and was temporarily stabilized with straw (Photo 17).-A material stockpile staged along the access road at STA 18+00 was bordered by reinforced silt fence and was temporarily stabilized with straw (Photo 18).-The plugging rig was installed at the time of inspection. All equipment was staged on the plugging pad. I was unable to see if secondary containment was installed at the plugging rig due to equipment being staged close to the rig (Photos 21-22).-The plugging pad perimeter was lined with reinforced silt fence, which appeared to be functioning properly. I observed no signs of accelerated erosion around the plugging pad (Photos 23-24).Due to sediment bypassing the silt fence at STA 14+00 and entering UNT to Dunkard Creek, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a)1, 78.53, CSL 301, and CSL 307(a) are being issued.

Report Details

Violation Date: 5/15/2025
Violation Code: 78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected.
Violation ID: 8233561
Permit API: 031-23676
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Monroe Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/15/2025
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an ongoing investigation into stray gas migration, involving combustible gas detected at the foundation of a nearby private residence. The well is situated approximately 650 feet north-northwest of the complainant’s residence. During the inspection, an updated well record was reviewed. The well was actively producing via the 4-inch production string, with valves on the 7-inch intermediate casing and the 4-inch production string annuls closed at the time of inspection Bubbling was observed in the annular space between the 9-5/8-inch surface casing and the 7-inch intermediate casing. Combustible gas screening using a calibrated gas meter indicated a concentration of 29% LEL (1.4%) in this annulus. According to the well records, both the 9-5/8-inch surface casing and the 7-inch intermediate casing were cemented to surface. The presence of combustible gas in the annulus suggests potential defects in the casing and/or cement integrity. Additionally, no check valve was observed on the production lines exiting the well. To further assess possible migration, four slam bar holes were installed approximately 6 inches to 1 foot from the wellhead in the cardinal directions, each about 3 feet deep. No detectable levels of combustible gas were found in the slam bar holes at the time of the inspection. A Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II meter, calibrated on 05/15/2025 was used for combustible gas screening during the inspection. It is noted that the operator has not responded to or completed the recommended corrective actions outlined in Inspection ID# 3913271. These actions were communicated via certified mail (USPS# 9589 0710 5270 1975 0616 42), sent on 02/13/2025 and received by the operator on 02/19/2025. As a result, the violations identified during this inspection are now being formally imposed on this well.

Report Details

Permit API: 081-21954
Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On September 26, 2024, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at the Beech Resources Delta Well Pad. No E and S issues were observed during the time of inspection. The site appeared to be stable and well vegetated meeting the 70% uniform perennial vegetative cover.Beech Resources contractors were in the process of setting up the well pad with production equipment and working on getting the AST ready for use. During the inspection, the east end of the well pad had some pools of water on it. The DEP screened the pool of water at the northeast corner with a conductivity meter. The conductivity meter measured the conductivity of the pool of water at 6,000 uS/cm. Near the pool of water in the northeast corner was a frack tank outside of containment. This frack tank contained water from the secondary containment of the drilling rig. Adjacent to the frack tank were multiple pallets of hoses used to manifold tanks together. The conductivity of the pool of water near and under the frack tank measured at 13,090 uS/cm. After observing the pools of water with elevated conductivity, the DEP went to the Company Man onsite and informed him of the findings. DEP showed the company where the pool of water was and the Company Man said that Beech Resources Don Stevenson was onsite. After finding Mr. Stevenson, DEP showed where the elevated conductivity pool was. Mr. Stevenson placed a call for a vac truck to mobilize to the well pad to removed the fluid. An excavator was used to dig a sump to collect the fluid so the vac truck could remove the fluid. Once the vac truck arrived onsite, Beech resources began removing the fluid from the sump and around the frack tank. The pallets of hoses were moved onto containment. During the removal of the fluid from the northeast corner conductivity was monitored in the fluid of the sump. Prior to DEP leaving the site, conductivity of the fluid in the sump measured at 3,900 uS/cm. Conductivity of the fluid was higher near the frack tank in the sump that was dug.At 1630 on September 26, 2024, Mr. Stevenson called DEP to inform them that all the fluid had been vacuumed and impacted soil had been removed. Mr. Stevenson said they were able to move the frack tank onto containment. After moving the frack tank, excavation of the impacted soil could begin. Mr. Stevenson said they removed approximately an excavator's bucket width for about 25 feet and removed about 6 inches of soil. Approximately 32 gallons of fluid was vacuumed and two roll off dumpsters were filled with impacted soil.Due to the amount of soil removed combined with the fluid vacuumed up Beech Resources has chosen to remediate to Act 2 standards. Violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.66(b)1, Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted.

Comments: On 03/12/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Morris F25 well site following violations issued on 12/19/2023 (IR 3662363, Enforcement 423308). I was accompanied by PA DEP Compliance Specialist, George Traister. Violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) were issued on 12/19/2023. The violations were issued as outstanding on 01/31/2024 (IR 3704581).The following was observed on 03/12/2024:Conductivity readings were taken within the water and gravel in the tank battery. The valve on Tank 1 looked to be leaking fluid. Crystallization was noted on the valve (Photo 1). The water within the battery around Tank 1 did not display elevated readings (Photo 2). The fluid escaping from the valve is recommended to be addressed. A reading was obtained within the gravel around the pan of Tank 4. This reading was 4.28 mS (Photo 3).Readings were taken within the gravel in the battery around Tank 5 and within the fluid in the pan. The readings within the gravel were 4.76 mS and 4.26 mS (Photos 4, 5). The reading within the pan was 17.30 mS (Photos 6, 7), which may indicate fluids leaking from tank fluid removal or from the valve itself. I recommend that this is addressed. The piping on the drain from the battery has been shortened. The exterior end is capped, and no elevated conductivity was noted on the ground below. The interior end is open, and I recommend that this is also capped. The water level in the battery is close to the edge of the pipe (Photos 8, 9). Stabilization has been added to the earthen berm. I recommend that additional is added as needed (Photos 10, 11).Pans are under each tank valve (Photo 12).Wet spots were noted on the exterior of the earthen berm. Conductivity readings were taken within these noted areas and resulted in the following: 4.00 mS, 6.33 mS, 5.44 mS. Another reading resulted in 1.15 mS. I recommend that fluid from inside the battery is not migrate through the berm. Livestock activity in the vicinity is taken into consideration (Photos 13-17). The violations issued on 12/29/2023 and 01/31/2024 remain outstanding.

Comments: Routine site inspection at conventional well 033-24249 on April 07, 2025. The well site is well vegetated. The well appears active and capable of producing. Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected. The brine tank is stationed in an earthen dike. Several inches of standing fluids was observed in the earthen dike. I screened in the fluids and found elevated conductance 10.01 mS/cm (photo 5). I screened outside the earthen dike using a soil probe and found elevated conductance ranging from 1.28 mS/cm -1.86 mS/cm (photos 7-9). The impacted area outside the earthen dike based off my soil field screening is approximately 25' long x 15'. Please note, there is a stream located approximately 35 yards away from the brine tank. I screened the stream for specific conductance and got a field reading of 26.5 uS/cm (photo 11). I collected a grab sample from the standing fluids within the earthen dike (photo 12). The sample 3442852 will be sent away to the DEP Lab and be tested for SAC 0942 plus aluminum, bromide, and lithium. I notified Diversified ESH Specialist Will Warfel via phone at ~1445 of my findings. Violations have been cited. The Department recommends that the operator address remediation of the spill/release in accordance with policy 800-5000-001 (Addressing Spills and Releases at O and G Well Sites or Access Roads).

Comments: On September 21, 2023, inspection conducted at the Rumpelstiltskin well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. The ERP was onsite (see photos 2 and 3). Some erosion rills were observed in the access road (see photos 4 and 5). Secondary containment was added to the GPU units onsite, and the impacted area was backfilled (see photos 10 and 11). A well tag was present on well 6H, with no observed leaks or discharge on the ground around it, and it appeared to be equipped for production (see photo 13). There are three other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photo 8). Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 12). Seven rolloff dumpsters labeled "production water impacted solids" were onsite (see photos 7 and 9). After inspection was conducted, the Department spoke via phone with EQT representative David Crayne, who stated that remediation was complete and Act 2 is nearly ready for submittal to ECB. Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that maintenance be conducted on the access road to prevent worsening accelerated erosion and sedimentation onsite. Closure of violations shall be contingent upon Act 2 approval and a subsequent CEI inspection.

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Violation ID: 8269860
Permit API: 039-24118
Unconventional: No

Municipality: East Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/01/2026
Comments: On 3/31/2026, Next Level Energy notified the Department that the Palermo 1 OG well (039-24118) sprayed an indeterminant amount of liquid mist out onto approximately of an acre while actively plugging the well. The Department dispatched Emergency Response to the site to evaluate.An onsite inspection in response to the complaint was conducted on 4/01/2026 by Elyse Henshaw, Water Quality Specialist, and Kyle Thomas, Oil and Gas Inspector. Upon arrival, Henshaw and Thomas found the impacted soil scraped up and piled around the well head. The soil was covered with tarps to prevent rainwater from carrying it from the site. Henshaw and Thomas conferred with representatives from Next Level Energy and Diversified to learn that the soil would be removed by the end of the week and plugging operations would resume. Henshaw and Thomas walked into the wooded area adjacent to the well site to find a waxy film on the leaf litter. Thomas believed the film was from the gel, a biodegradable material, used to put down hole to kill the well rather than residual crude oil. Henshaw and a representative from Diversified walked into the wooded area to determine the extent of the spray and did not find a sheen on top of the puddles within the area. Additionally, they utilized conductivity probes to determine no brine water was sprayed into the woods. They also tested multiple points in the area that had been scraped up to determine all contaminated soils had been removed. A small amount of brine water remained around the well head and will be removed when plugging operations conclude. Fresh topsoil, seed and mulch will be brought in to stabilize and restore the impacted area. On 04/07/2026 a copy of this report was sent to Diversified Production LLC at painspections@dgoc.com for their review.

Comments: This inspection is taking place as a follow up to IR 3129333 which documented an operator reported release of fluid from a GPU to the ground on 12/23/2020. The following is observed: The Act 9 sign is present and appears to be in good condition (Photo 1). The ERP, PPC, and associated safety data sheets are present in the mailbox. The GPU's do not appear to be in secondary containment (Photo 2), per the COA signed on 12/17/2020, this is being noted as ICS. The sump is still present adjacent to the GPU (Photo 3), conductivity readings taken in and around the sump read in the 60-70 uS range. Based on the on-site conditions, the site does not appear to have been remediated. Mr. Lance Witters with EQT was spoken to by phone, he confirmed that the site is still being remediated under 78a.66c(1). Mr. Witters was advised that under the previsions of 91.33(B) the site should be remediated by no later than 1/7/2020. Mr. Witters stated that a follow up by the operator will be conducted to evaluate the remediation effort. No migration of impacted material to stormwater management facilities or WOTC is observed. The roll off box with impacted material is still present on the pad (Photo 4). Based on this inspection violations noted in IR 3129333 remain outstanding. Pending a follow up inspection, more violations may be forthcoming. The Department requests the waste manifest once it is available.

Comments: On April 6th, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a complaint received for the Schimizzi S&M1 Well Site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. Well label with operator information is faded and needs updated, as recommended in IR 3262201. Earthen berm around production tank appeared to be stable and well vegetated. Towards the bottom of the 1st production tank, there was a pin hole actively leaking production fluid to the ground (photo 7). There were several animal burrows around the base of both tanks. Conductivity readings were collected at several locations around the well site (photo 5 - 15). Collected readings as follows: East side of tank 2 (Or), south side of tank 1 (2.35 mS), west side of tank 1 (Or), north side of tank 1 (0.57 mS), west side of tank 2 (0.45 mS), Hole 6 (0.21 mS), Hole 5 (0.24 mS), Hole 4 (0.23 mS), Hole 3 (0.21 mS), Hole 2 (0.20 mS), Hole 1 (0.06 mS). Based on today's inspection and conductivity readings, additional violations are being issued. All violations cited in IR 3174464 and IR 3262201 will remain outstanding.

Unconventional: No

Comments: Arrived at location on 8/9/2022 to met with Operator representative, Matt Kleese (Diamond Energy), late afternoon with cool, cloudy weather conditions, and 65 degrees. The wellhead, unions, valves, and tubulars replaced and plumbed (photos #1 and #2). All old parts and materials disposed of due to fire damage. Minor leak at lower casing collar union continues after rebuilding of wellhead (photo #3). Operator will address/repair this union leak tomorrow (8/10/22) by entering the well with tubing, secure well and make repair to casing collar union at wellhead. The well is being vented/produced to sales line and recorded on a newly installed 31-day production chart (photo #4). Utilizing the 100 bbl steel tank at the ground production facility as additional vent for spill prevention. The tank vent is open to atmosphere (photo #5). Routine and complete inspection in response to incident of well catching fire after a lightning strike that was witnessed by the property land owner during a thunderstorm on August 5, 2022 at approximately 2042 hours. Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8207455
Permit API: 113-20465
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Cherry Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/12/2024
Comments: Site inspection conducted by EPS Justin Abbott at the Yonkin Well Pad in response to a spill notification submitted by CHK (aka Expand Energy) for a spill detected at 1300 hours on 11/11/24. Meeting on site today with CHK Consultant Brett Fowler. Weather conditions at time of inspection are overcast and 39 degrees F. According to the Emergency Response Notification Report at 1300 hours the following occurred, "up welling of pad adjacent to well head caused concern; Expand started digging at on 11/11/24 at 1:00 p.m.; Expand Energy started digging and encountered produced water with a conductivity of 8000 s/cm. Source of produced water is unknown. Ms. Schaad said that the produced water was not coming up from around the well casing. Expand Energy has Creston Environmental on site utilizing a vac truck to empty excavation. Ms. Schaad said that a small volume of produced water (greater than 5 gallons) has been recovered."At time of inspection, the Department observed a trench dug adjacent to the 5HC well in the affected area. The Department conducted conductivity screenings of the affected area using an Oakton PCTS 50 meter and a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity meter. Puddled fluid collected in the trench in the affected area was observed with electrical conductivity readings of 3.24 mS/cm. The trenched area of the reported spill was approximately 12' long by 6' wide and 4' deep where water is puddled (photo 4). In a followup conversation with Danielle Schaad, HSE Representative for Chesapeake, the following information was relayed regarding the cause of the spill: the spill of production fluid was observed to be caused by a torn seam in the secondary containment structure which was not apparent until rig mats and containment were removed. Approximately one barrel of fluid was vacuumed from the trench and 14 cubic yards of impacted pad rock were removed from the trench. CHK has contracted with Creston Environmental to pursue Act 2 site characterization. According to Mr. Fowler, Nine Energy Services is conducting wireline operations to change out a valve on the 23HC well (API#113-20465). Plugs have been drilled out, but the wells are shut in and no production equipment has yet been set up on this pad. Rig mats are also observed being stacked and removed from the location at time of inspection. A supersucker vacuum truck is observed on site removing high conductivity fluids from the impacted rock stockpiled in the northwest corner of the pad (photo 5). Additional puddles with elevated conductivity readings ranging from 2.2-2.7 mS/cm were observed (photo 6) where impacted pad rock is stockpiled. The Department recommends vacuuming fluid from surface puddles adjacent to the stockpile. During site walk, the Department inspected downslope areas of the well pad to determine if fluid was released from the pad surface. No indication of off-pad release was observed. Violations noted. Violations remain outstanding against API# 113-20470 for SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b) dated 9/23/24.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/01/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's DCNR 587 02-003 well site located in Ward Township, Tioga County on 2/1/2023 at 1540 hours. The weather was 26 degrees with clear skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a reported release called in by Repsol.On 2/1/2023 at ~1335 hours, a release of ~5 barrels of produced water, ice and sand was discovered by Repsol after a line on a sand trap froze and split. Water, ice and sand was release to the pad surface near the wellheads onsite (photos #1 and 2). Sand, ice and dirt was recovered and placed in a 55-gallon drum for later disposal. The release mixed with onsite stormwater that was held in and around the well cellars. An onsite vacuum truck recovered a reported 1000 gallons of stormwater mixed with the produced water from the cellars and impacted area. I field measured all of the fluids in and around the impacted area for electrical conductivity utilizing an Oakton PCTS 50 meter. All readings ranged from 400 to 680us/cm today. Based on the reported release of ~5 barrels of produced water to the pad surface, new violations of the following are cited against API #117-22101 at this time:35 P.S. 691.402(b)25 Pa. Code78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.301Violations cited against API #117-22101 on 7/27/2022 remain outstanding at this time. I departed the site at 1615 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/21/2023
Violation Code: 78.64(d)1 - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator drained tank containment facilities which caused a harmful discharge or resulted in a sheen.
Violation ID: 8153359
Permit API: 121-45433
Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Sugarcreek Borough
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/21/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023.There is an active discharge of fluid from the Tank Battery of the Lower Reno oil lease that is permitted and operated by Petro Erie Inc.. The public water supply for the town of Reno, PA is under a "Do Not Consume Advisory" based upon an increase in TDS for the Bellows Spring Cistern (owned and operated by Venango Water Company).The tank battery consists of (2) 210bbl steel tanks and (4) 100bbl poly tanks. The earthen dike appears to be lined with a plastic liner. There is a dike drain that is located in the southwest corner of the dike. The valve on the drain pipe is open and fluid is flowing to the ground. The area inside the dike appears to have been impacted by produced fluid from the tanks. A pipeline between two of the poly tanks was actively dripping fluid. Field screening inside the dike were conducted with the soil probe for conductivity, and all readings were above the range of the meter (20,000uS).The discharge from the dike drain flows south across an open area and into a wooded area. There is a visible impact area extending from the dike drain in an irregular pattern approximately 80 yards from the earthen dike and approximately ranging from 6' to 25' in width. Field screening within the impacted area was conducted approximately every 10 yards. Conductivity measurements ranged from 11,000uS to above the range of the meter (20,000uS). Several areas outside of the impacted area were checked with the soil probe and the levels ranged between 60uS to 164uS. An oil sheen is visible within the flowing water and dead vegetation is also observed including several large cherry trees within the impacted area. The amount of discharged fluid is unknown and based upon the observations onsite it appears that the discharge has been occurring for some time.The dike drain was closed by DEP staff at 8:45am to stop the continued discharge of fluid outside of the earthen dike.Water samples were collected at the dike drain outlet (discharge point) and sent to the lab for analysis. Water samples were also collected at the Bellows Spring Cistern (41.422360 -79.764490) which is a source for a public water supply of the town of Reno, PA.While onsite the Department talked with the operator/owner (Harry Rhoades) via a phone conversation. The discharge and the potential that the discharge may be impacting the public water supply was discussed with Mr. Rhoades. Mr. Rhoades insisted that he does not discharge his brine and that he could provide disposal documents. It was stated that the dike drain was left open because of forecasted rain. Violations are cited.The Oil and Gas Inspector (OGI) will be conducting a separate well compliance inspection for the well and other wells on the lease.
